attributes.body_ja:
「それなのに」は、代名詞（だいめいし）「それ」に「な」と逆接（ぎゃくせつ）を表（あらわ）す助詞（じょし）「のに」を加（くわ）えた表現（ひょうげん）です。これは「しかし」や「にもかかわらず」と同（おな）じように、前（まえ）に述（の）べられたことと、逆（ぎゃく）のことを述（の）べるときに使（つか）われる接続詞（せつぞくし）です。

「それなのに」は接続詞（せつぞくし）なので、主（おも）に文（ぶん）の頭（あたま）に置（お）かれます。

(A) の内容（ないよう）と (B) の内容（ないよう）は逆接（ぎゃくせつ）の関係（かんけい）にあるので、「それなのに」は (A) を考（かんが）えると起（お）こるはずのないことや、予想外（よそうがい）のことを表（あらわ）すためによく使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
Being a combination of the substitute noun それ, な, and のに, the particle meaning 'although' or 'despite', それなのに acts as a conjunction meaning 'and yet', or 'despite that', and simply refers back to the previous statement made, when the following statement is in contradiction to it.

Due to its use as a conjunction, それなのに will primarily appear at the beginning of a new sentence.

Being that the (B) sentence is in contradiction to the (A) sentence, それなのに will often indicate something that is unexpected, or was somehow unpredictable based on (A).

Both introduce contradiction. それにしても can mean even so or nevertheless, and can also be used to change topics, as in それにしても暑いね (Even so, it’s hot, isn’t it?). それなのに marks direct contrast, closer to and yet, as in 一生懸命勉強した。それなのに落ちた (I studied hard, and yet I failed).

Both can begin a sentence to introduce contrast, but differ in tone and nuance. もっとも is more formal and adds a condition that qualifies the previous statement, e.g. 全員来ました。もっとも、田中さんは遅れましたが 'Everyone came. That said, Tanaka was late.' それなのに is more casual and expresses surprise at an unexpected outcome, e.g. 雨だった。それなのに、試合は行われた 'It rained. And yet, the match was held.'

first_relatable.title: もっとも
first_relatable.meaning: Although, But, However, For all that, Provided that

attributes.body: Both express contrast, but with different nuances and usage. ながらも attaches to verbs, adjectives, or nouns and conveys contradictory states, e.g. '緊張しながらもわくわくしている' ('While feeling anxious, I'm also excited'). それなのに is used at the start of a sentence to mean 'and yet', often with surprise, e.g. '８時間も寝た。それなのに眠い' ('I slept eight whole hours. But still, I'm sleepy').

first_relatable.title: ながらも
first_relatable.meaning: But, Even while, Even though, Despite, Although

attributes.body: Both introduce contrast. しかしながら is formal and neutral, used in writing or speeches, as in 実験は失敗した。しかしながら多くを学んだ (The experiment failed. Nevertheless, we learned a lot). それなのに is conversational and conveys surprise or disappointment, as in 約束した。それなのに来なかった (He promised, and yet he didn’t come).

Both express contrast, but differ in usage and implication. くせに follows a phrase and has a critical tone, e.g. 知っているくせに教えてくれない ('He knows but won't tell me.'), implying that the speaker is angry at the person. それなのに comes at the beginning of a sentence, is neutral, and expresses simple contradiction, e.g. 彼は真実を知っている。それなのに、教えてくれない ('He knows. And yet, he won't tell me.') with an objective nuance.

のに expresses contrast, similar to 'although,' and follows verbs, adjectives, or nouns (with な for nouns and な-adjectives). It's typically used at the end of a phrase or sentence. それなのに is a related form used at the beginning of a sentence, meaning 'and yet' or 'despite that,' with それ referring back to the previous statement.

それでも and それなのに both show contrast. それでも means 'even so' and sounds neutral, e.g. 雨だった。それでも行った ('It was rainy, but I went anyway.'). それなのに has a stronger emotional tone, often of disbelief or disapproval, e.g. 優しくした。それなのに怒られた ('I was nice and still got yelled at!').

first_relatable.title: それでも
first_relatable.meaning: But still, And yet, Even so, Nevertheless
